spec_match.rationale: Probes the exact [Exposed] contract — five CSSStyleValue hierarchy constructors across Window, dedicated worker and module worker, each context reporting on itself — plus a real construction check distinguishing defined from usable.

interactive.rationale: Auto-runs on load and offers Run again; workers are genuinely spawned from blob URLs and their reports fill the matrix live.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises the same probe in three scopes with nothing inferred from the window, and that is the page.

edge_cases.rationale: Worker spawn failure, worker timeout, and the exists-but-unusable constructor case each have a distinct row/state, and the construction error is surfaced verbatim.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5146996093616128's sibling — https://chromestatus.com/feature/5114591051907072 — and the Typed OM StyleValue subclasses section.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite asserts worker exposure, in-worker construction, parse and unit conversion; on Chromium 141 the route honestly reported 2 pass / 5 fail — precisely the pre-154 window-only exposure this page visualises.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): the probe ran live and showed the historical bug exactly — Window column all yes, both worker columns all no, 10 of 15 cells missing, worker TypeError surfaced; console clean, no failed same-origin requests, desktop and mobile screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and emits a contexts-probed assert with per-context usability.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, emerald/rose verdicts as text plus colour, focusable code block, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: Captioned matrix with scoped row/column headers, aria-live detail, summary state as text beside an aria-hidden icon, single labelled button.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: At 360x740 DPR3 the document scrollWidth is 389px: the four-column matrix forces horizontal overflow and the 360px screenshot shows the module-worker column, the summary banner text and the stage border clipped at the right edge.

openQuestions.title: Fix the 360px horizontal overflow of the context matrix
openQuestions.detail: The results table has no overflow-wrap:anywhere (unlike the sibling parse-in-a-worker page, which stays at 360px) and its mono headers ('dedicated worker', 'module worker') push the layout to 389px at a 360px viewport, clipping the last column, the summary banner and the stage border. Add overflow-wrap:anywhere to th/td and let the header text wrap, or give the table an internal horizontal scroll container, then re-verify with the responsive matrix (deno task responsive-check).

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/expose-cssstylevalue-hierarchy-to-worker-contexts/context-probe/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp). This build predates the feature, so the live matrix showed the exact gap being closed — Window all-yes, both worker columns all-no with the worker's own TypeError quoted — which is the ideal honest state for this demo, and the console stayed clean. Feature /conformance/ honestly reported 2 pass / 5 fail (window exposure passes, worker exposure fails pre-154). The one real defect is responsive: at 360px the matrix overflows to 389px and clips its right edge, confirmed by scrollWidth measurement and the mobile screenshot, so mobile_desktop_parity fails until the table wraps or scrolls internally.
